title: cost_report.json
description: Phase 13 comprehensive cost, scalability, and deployment evaluation report
consumers: Phase 9 - Experiment Planner (feedback loop for improved resource estimation)

performance_summary._comment: Produced by: Phase 10 execution. Consumed by: Phase 13 (correlates performance with cost)

training._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 Resource Profiler. Consumed by: Phase 13 cost estimator, Phase 9 (improved future estimates)

inference._comment: Inference cost matters for deployment at scale

quantum_cost._comment: Produced by: Phase 10 quantum runtime. Consumed by: Phase 13 (quantum workload quantification), cloud cost estimator

storage_cost._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 storage monitor. Consumed by: deployment planner

financial_cost_local._comment: Local execution: financial cost ≈ 0, but resource usage ≠ 0. Produced by: Phase 13 cost estimator.

financial_cost_cloud_estimate.note: Cloud cost estimation requires selected provider pricing. Example: AWS, IBM Quantum, Azure Quantum.
financial_cost_cloud_estimate._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 cloud cost estimator (when provider configured). Consumed by: business decision layer

dataset_size_scaling.growth_trend: Approximately linear time scaling with sample count. Performance plateaus after 500 samples.
dataset_size_scaling._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 scalability module. Consumed by: Phase 9 (decides subset strategy for large datasets)

feature_scaling.growth_trend: Exponential memory scaling with qubit count. Diminishing performance returns beyond 8 qubits.
feature_scaling.recommendation: 8 qubits optimal for this dataset - balances performance and resource cost.
feature_scaling._comment: Feature reduction (Phase 6) is NOT optional decoration - it makes quantum branch computationally feasible

circuit_depth_scaling.recommendation: Depth 2 optimal - depth 4/6 provide negligible improvement at 2-4× cost
circuit_depth_scaling._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 circuit depth analyzer. Consumed by: Phase 8 (quantum model configuration)

shots_scaling.recommendation: 1024 shots provides stable measurement estimates. 2048 minimal improvement at 33% cost increase.
shots_scaling._comment: More shots = more stable estimate but higher execution cost

resource_feasibility.scaling_limit: 16 qubits feasible with high resource usage. 32 qubits NOT recommended.
resource_feasibility._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 feasibility analyzer. Consumed by: Phase 9 (filters infeasible configurations)

performance_vs_cost._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 Pareto analyzer. Consumed by: Frontend (performance-cost curve), reports (practical recommendations)

comparison_classical_baseline.verdict: Classical XGBoost superior in both performance (2% higher AUC) and cost (18× faster). Quantum NOT advantageous for this dataset/configuration.
comparison_classical_baseline._comment: Honest comparison - quantum not always better. Produced by: Phase 13. Consumed by: Phase 11 (recommendation), reports

reasons: Classical baseline outperforms quantum in both accuracy and speed
Quantum training 18× slower with marginal performance gap
8-qubit VQC suitable for research/validation, not production deployment
deployment_recommendation.alternative: Deploy XGBoost (EXP-C-000001) for production. Use quantum for continued research.
deployment_recommendation._comment: Produced by: Phase 13 deployment evaluator. Consumed by: business decision layer, final reports

backend_compatibility.migration_effort: LOW - same experiment config, change backend_type only
backend_compatibility._comment: Backend abstraction allows future hardware/cloud migration without code rewrite

pipeline_cost_breakdown._comment: Quantum training dominates pipeline cost. CNN feature extraction would dominate for image datasets.

caching_effectiveness._comment: Caching prevents repeated computation across experiments

field_definitions.computational_cost.training.cpu_time_sec: float: Total CPU time across all cores
field_definitions.quantum_cost.total_circuit_executions: integer: Number of times quantum circuit was executed during training
field_definitions.scalability_analysis.growth_trend: string: Linear, exponential, logarithmic - describes resource scaling behavior
field_definitions.performance_vs_cost.pareto_efficient: boolean: Whether this config is on Pareto frontier (no other config dominates it)
field_definitions.performance_vs_cost.dominated_by: string or null: Experiment ID that provides better/equal performance at lower/equal cost
field_definitions.comparison_classical_baseline.verdict: string: Honest assessment - classical may be superior
field_definitions.backend_compatibility.migration_effort: enum: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH - effort to migrate to cloud/hardware backend
field_definitions.pipeline_cost_breakdown: object: Shows which pipeline stage dominates cost (quantum training, CNN extraction, etc.)

notes: Phase 13 answers: 'Can this system be used at scale, and what does it cost?'
Honest comparison: quantum NOT always better - this report doesn't hide classical superiority
Scalability testing shows growth trends - exponential memory for qubits, linear for samples
Feature reduction (Phase 6) is what makes quantum branch feasible - not optional
Pareto frontier identifies practical sweet spots - best performance for given cost
deployment_recommendation may say 'use classical' - platform honesty is strength
Backend abstraction means same experiment_config can target local_sim/cloud_sim/hardware
Pipeline cost breakdown reveals bottleneck - may be CNN feature extraction, not quantum
Financial cost ≈ 0 for local execution, but resource usage ≠ 0 (CPU, RAM, electricity)
Cloud cost estimation requires provider pricing - example providers: IBM Quantum, AWS Braket, Azure Quantum
Phase 13 → Phase 9 feedback loop: actual costs improve future resource estimates
This report connects to SIH concern: 'What about cost? What is in it for people?'
Platform demonstrates: quantum MAY provide value for specific datasets/configs, but classical remains strong baseline
Scalability modes: LOCAL (dev/small datasets) → GPU/HPC (larger workloads) → CLOUD_SIMULATOR → HARDWARE
Resource-aware scheduling prevents runaway experiments - execution_budget enforced
Caching (CNN embeddings, PCA transformations, kernel matrices) dramatically reduces repeated computation
